programme: Loss of PML-nuclear-body checkpoint activity: PML acting on its growth-arrest/apoptosis targets (TP53, BAX, CASP3, CDKN1A, EGFR, FLT3, CCND1) is the only factor in this set with a documented, disease-specific mechanism in the retrieved material. The other eleven concordant factors fall into unrelated programmes with no evidence linking them to each other or to this pair: RORC anchors a Th17/Treg differentiation signature (IL17A, IL17F, IL22, IL23R, RORA, FOXP3, CCR6, IL21); FOXJ1 anchors motile-ciliogenesis genes (DNAH11, DNAI1, DNALI1, TEKT2, CETN2, ASPM); TET1 carries DNA-demethylation/neural-differentiation targets; NFIA carries glial-specification targets; ZNF451 acts on SMAD2/SMAD4; EWSR1 carries a broad sarcoma-fusion transcriptional target set. None of these five converge with PML or with each other.
role_in_a: In the blood network for Intellectual_Disability, PML's checkpoint targets (TP53, BAX, CASP3, CDKN1A) sit downstream of a documented route to disease: a retrieved paper places PML in an interaction with CMV-encoded immediate-early protein that perturbs neural progenitor proliferation, a mechanism relevant to congenital CMV-associated intellectual disability.
role_in_b: In the uveal network for Ocular_Melanomas, a retrieved paper places PML as a target of ALKBH3-mediated m1A demethylation (boosted by histone lactylation), with PML diminishment associated with tumor progression in high-risk disease — consistent with PML acting as a tumor-suppressor checkpoint that is removed rather than activated.
shared_axis: Both settings converge on suppression of PML-nuclear-body checkpoint activity rather than its induction — sequestration by a viral protein in one context, enzymatic destabilization in the other — each removing a brake on proliferation in its respective cell type. No source states this as a connection between the two diseases; it is inferred from the fact that each disease separately documents a PML-loss mechanism.
reasoning: PML is the only one of twelve factors with disease-specific mechanistic placement in both A and B, which meets the bar for 'supported' (each disease separately known to involve the programme) rather than 'established' (no source states the pair together) or 'unexpected' (there is documentation, just not joint). Strength is capped at moderate because only one factor carries the story, the two documented mechanisms are structurally different (protein interaction vs. RNA modification), and the inference that they represent the 'same' loss-of-checkpoint axis is mine, not stated in either paper.
support: PMID 41655694 — in Intellectual_Disability, CMV-encoded immediate-early 1 protein perturbs neural progenitor proliferation via an interaction reported for PML. PMID 38118002 — in Ocular_Melanomas, histone lactylation-boosted ALKBH3 diminishes PML via m1A modification, associated with tumor progression in high-risk disease.
how_to_falsify: Measure PML protein/activity in blood or neural tissue from patients with CMV-associated (or other) intellectual disability to confirm it is actually reduced, and separately test whether ALKBH3 knockdown restores PML levels and suppresses proliferation in uveal melanoma lines. If PML is not depleted in the intellectual-disability context, or restoring PML does not blunt uveal melanoma proliferation, the shared loss-of-checkpoint account fails.
caveats: Blood (disease A) and uvea (disease B) are anatomically and functionally unrelated compartments, and this pair rests on only 12 patient-group comparisons from 2 independent cohort pairs — a modest base. Common blood/immune TFs (KLF2, FOXO1/3/4, ETS1, BCL6, PBX1, NR4A3) were already removed as tissue-generic, so RORC's Th17 signature is specific rather than generic to blood, but it carries no documented tie to either disease and should not be read as an immune mechanism for this pair. Literature placement in Intellectual_Disability alone (NFIA, TET1, ENO1, and PML) likely reflects that intellectual disability is better studied in the retrieval corpus than ocular melanoma, not that those factors are more biologically relevant here; only PML has any placement on the Ocular_Melanomas side.
